steps.what: List the facts already on the case
Draft questions from the logged facts

loop.input: fact ids and the question template
loop.output: questions that each cite one fact id
loop.check: Every question cites a fact id on the list and none states a finding of guilt
loop.stop: If the fact list is empty, return no questions and stop
loop.why_not_simpler: How to ask about a contradiction is not a fixed table

steps.what: Interview the person and take notes
Write each answer against its question
Decide the referral, ban or sanction
Send the signed referral or sanction

tasks.design: The investigator lists fact ids already on the {WORKFLOW} case. A bounded note in {DOCS} drafts questions that cite those ids only, and the interview stays in the room. The manager signs one referral, ban or sanction version, and only that version is sent. The draft does not decide guilt.
tasks.previous_blocker: Facts sat in notebooks, so a referral pack could not show which case id it relied on.
tasks.enabler_now: A case can hold fact ids, a person role and a store id that a question list and a referral can both cite.
tasks.still_hard: What someone says in the room, and whether it is enough to refer or sanction, is not a rule.
tasks.human_edge: The manager conducts the interview and signs any referral, ban or sanction.

ambition.what: Sign the referral or sanction on the day of the interview instead of in a later batch

tasks.altitude: The question list is ready before the interview. The conversation and the outcome stay the manager's, and an unsigned pack is not sent.

reach.task: Prepare the fact list for a theft interview
reach.learn: Which fact ids are already logged and which outcome version was signed

evidence.claim: The interview is the task. The fact list before it and the referral after it are the only parts with a stable shape.
Digest [S9] says decisions about people must not rest on automation alone. A referral, ban or sanction is signed by the manager.

Digest [S12] says works council consent is required for staff monitoring. An internal-theft interview names staff and starts from an open case, not from covert watching. A shoplifting interview of a customer is not staff monitoring.
Digest [S15] says a paid report drafted with a model cited sources that did not exist. Questions and the referral may cite only fact ids already on the case.
Digest [S3] says incident reports are forwarded to the person in charge. The external pack goes only after signature, to the recipient named on the case.

assumptions: Focal role is the loss prevention manager. The task runs from an open case to a signed interview outcome. Opening the case is a prior task.

Input contract: case id, person role (customer or staff), fact ids, store id, interview time, location. Producer of the fact list is the investigator. If there is no case id, the question draft does not run and the interview stays fully manual.
Use the case form and the document template before custom code. The send step uses the mail tool's own template.
This is not covert surveillance and it produces no suspicion score. Interview and note-taking time stays with the people in the room. A sanction or external referral uses the signed version only.
unknowns: Whether works-council consent covers interview notes that name staff.
Who receives a police referral at each site.
Who may sign when the manager is absent.
research_questions: What share of interviews start with no case id?
How often is a signed referral later withdrawn?

already_counted.description: Manager edits questions that do not match the facts
Interview time stays with the manager
Referral and sanction judgement stays with the manager

incremental.description: Keep the question template aligned with the case fact fields
Investigators repair fact lists the draft rejects

approvals.approved_version: referral, ban or sanction version signed for this interview

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes most interviews have no fact list, so the question draft rarely runs and the room time is unchanged. The high case assumes a clean case file, but every interview and every referral or sanction still takes the manager's time. No unattended referral is in scope.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Recommend actions in a store crisis

steps.what: Report the store, time and crisis type
Open the plan for this crisis type
Draft the recommendation from logged facts

loop.input: plan steps and logged crisis facts
loop.output: recommendation that cites plan step ids or fact lines
loop.check: Every action cites a plan step id or a fact line in the report
loop.stop: If the type has no plan, return an empty draft and stop
loop.why_not_simpler: What is safe to do in this incident is not a lookup on the type alone

steps.what: Sign the recommendation for this crisis
Talk the store through the signed actions
File the signed recommendation and date

tasks.design: The store supervisor reports store id, time and crisis type on a {WORKFLOW} form. The manager opens the matching plan in {DOCS}, and a bounded note drafts a recommendation that cites only that plan and the logged facts. The manager signs one version, talks the store through it, and files it with a review date on the {CALENDAR}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Crisis notes were a phone call and a later mail, so the recommendation could not show which plan step it used.
tasks.enabler_now: A short plan library can be keyed by crisis type, and the first report can carry store id, time and type as fields.
tasks.still_hard: A live incident does not follow the plan, and the people on the call still have to judge what is safe.
tasks.human_edge: The manager signs the recommendation and talks the store through what to do now.

ambition.what: Review each crisis plan on its review date instead of only after the next incident

tasks.altitude: The plan is open before the advice is given. The call stays the manager's, and a recommendation with no plan id is not filed.

reach.task: Carry out the signed crisis actions in the store
reach.learn: Which recommendation version was signed and which plan steps were refused

evidence.claim: Crisis calls are rare. The conversation stays. A short plan library is the part that can be prepared before the next call.
Digest [S15] says a paid report drafted with a model cited sources that did not exist. The recommendation is not sent until the manager checks every cited plan step.
Digest [S3] says incident reports go to the person in charge. The store report is routed to the manager. It is not answered by the draft.
Digest [S8] says a larger incident register is more reporting, not fewer incidents. A filed crisis note is not evidence that the next event will be smaller.

assumptions: Focal role is the loss prevention manager. The task ends when a signed recommendation is filed with a review date. Running a full exercise is a later task.

Input contract: store id, crisis type, start time, police-called flag, short fact text. Producer is the store supervisor. An unknown type skips the draft and the manager writes the recommendation by hand.
Use the document store's plan templates and the workflow form before custom code.
The meeting prior is real. The call and the decision stay. This is not staff monitoring. The recommendation is advice for the incident, not a sanction and not an automated decision about a person.
unknowns: Which crisis types have no plan yet.
Whether local police expect a named contact on the recommendation.
Who may sign if the manager cannot be reached.
research_questions: How many crisis types have a plan with a review date?
How often does the signed version drop steps that were in the draft?

already_counted.description: Manager cuts draft lines that the plan does not support
The decision on the call stays with the manager
Talking the store through the actions stays with the manager

incremental.description: Add a plan when a crisis type repeats and has no entry
Store supervisors correct a report filed under the wrong type

approvals.approved_version: crisis recommendation version signed for this report

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes most events have no matching plan, so the draft does not run and the call is unchanged. The high case assumes a plan exists, but the decision and the conversation still take the manager's time. The on-site response by store staff is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Find loss patterns and write a strategy

steps.what: Open shrink and stock-gap rows
Flag stores and groups over the threshold
Draft strategies from the flagged rows

loop.input: flagged rows and the strategy template
loop.output: actions that cite store id and period
loop.check: Every action cites a store id on the flagged list and names no person
loop.stop: Stop after one draft and drop any sentence with no store id
loop.why_not_simpler: Which action a store can staff is not in the extract

steps.what: Decide which actions to adopt
Comment on what the store can do
File the signed strategy version

tasks.design: A {BI} view shows shrink, voids and stock gaps by store and product group from the {OPS_SYSTEM}. Fixed thresholds flag rows over the band. A bounded note in {DOCS} drafts actions that cite those rows only. The manager signs one strategy version. The note does not name a person as the cause.
tasks.previous_blocker: Shrink figures were rebuilt in a workbook for each review, so a proposed action could not point at a store row.
tasks.enabler_now: Stock and till totals can be exported by store, period and product group with a threshold id.
tasks.still_hard: Which loss to attack first is a trade-off with store operations, not a sort of the largest number.
tasks.human_edge: The manager chooses which actions to adopt and which to drop.

ambition.what: Revisit a store strategy when its shrink band changes, not only in the yearly plan

tasks.altitude: Collecting the figures shrinks. The choice of what to stop, and the conversation with the store, stay with the manager.

reach.task: Say which signed actions the store can run
reach.learn: Which strategy version applies and which rows were over the threshold

evidence.claim: Strategies in this job start from shrink and stock rows. Choosing what to change is still a judgement with the store.
Digest [S8] says a larger register is more reporting, not proof that loss fell. A longer list of flagged stores is not a result of the strategy.
Digest [S15] says a paid report drafted with a model cited sources that did not exist. The strategy note may cite only row ids on the flagged list.
Digest [S2] says a GRC platform has audit modules that can hold actions as a register. That is not shop-floor watching.
Digest [S12] says works council consent is required for staff monitoring. This note cites store metrics only. Ranking employees would be a different design and is out of scope.

assumptions: Focal role is the loss prevention manager. The task ends when a strategy version is signed and filed. Carrying out the actions in store is later work.
Input contract: store id, period, shrink amount, product group, void count, stock-gap amount, threshold id. Producer is the operations export. A row with no store id is dropped and not cited.
Use the existing operations report and dashboard filters before custom code.
The meeting prior is partly the decision conversation, which stays. Exception queries are operational rows, not a hidden watch of named people. No person id enters the strategy note.
unknowns: Which product groups are stable enough to trend.
Who owns an action that sits with a supplier rather than a store.
Whether finance uses the same shrink definition.
research_questions: What share of stores changes shrink band between monthly extracts?
How often does the signed version drop the draft's largest row?

already_counted.description: Manager edits actions the rows do not support
Strategy decision time stays with the manager

incremental.description: Revise threshold bands when the shrink definition changes
Store supervisors correct a product group on a flagged row

approvals.approved_version: strategy version signed for this period

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes the export is not grouped by store, so the flags rarely fire and the manager still builds the brief by hand. The high case assumes clean rows, but every strategy choice and every store conversation still takes manager time. No reduction in loss is treated as time saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Hire and supervise loss prevention staff

steps.what: Draft the vacancy from the role template

loop.input: role template fields and the vacancy sections
loop.output: vacancy text that cites template fields only
loop.check: Every requirement cites a template field and none is a trait score
loop.stop: Stop if the role id is missing
loop.why_not_simpler: Local site conditions are not all in the template

steps.what: Sign the vacancy version
Post the signed vacancy
Interview the candidates in person
Decide the hire and sign the offer
Send the signed offer
Supervise staff in the weekly meeting
Bring the week's open case list

tasks.design: The manager drafts a vacancy from the role template in the {ATS} and signs that version before it is posted. Interviews stay in the room. A hire and an offer are signed by the manager, and only that offer version is sent. The weekly supervision meeting stays a conversation. No trait score is produced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Vacancies and offers were rewritten in mail, so a posted role could drift from the template the manager had agreed.
tasks.enabler_now: The recruitment system can hold a role id, a site and an offer version, and the meeting can sit on a case list rather than a blank agenda.
tasks.still_hard: Whether someone should be hired, and how to supervise them, is a judgement about a person.
tasks.human_edge: The manager decides the hire, signs the offer, and runs the supervision meeting.
tasks.altitude: The vacancy and the offer have a version. Interviews and supervision do not move. The manager can refuse an offer that does not match the signed vacancy.

reach.task: Bring the open case list to supervision
reach.learn: Which vacancy version is posted and which offer version was signed

evidence.claim: Hiring and supervision in this job are conversations. The vacancy and the offer are the documents that can carry a version.
Digest [S10] and [S11] say the AI Act Annex III includes hiring, evaluating or rostering staff on behaviour or traits. This design does not score candidates or staff. A person decides the hire.
Digest [S9] says decisions about people must not rest on automation alone. The offer is signed by the manager and is not an automated decision.
Digest [S12] says works council consent is required for staff data and rosters. The vacancy uses candidate and staff data, so consent and access are a precondition. This task does not build a roster.

assumptions: Focal role is the loss prevention manager. The task covers the vacancy, the interviews, the offer and the weekly supervision meeting. Payroll setup is out of scope.

Input contract: role id, site id, contract type, candidate id, interview date, offer amount band. Producer of the role need is the manager. Producer of applications is the recruitment system. A missing role id stops the vacancy draft.
Use the recruitment system's own templates and approval flow before custom code.

No trait score and no covert monitoring of the team. Interview and supervision time is not saved. Works-council consent for candidate data is settled before go-live. The meeting prior is accepted for this task.
unknowns: Whether the works council must consent before a named attendance or candidate list is stored.
Who may sign an offer when the manager is away.
Which sites hire through a shared recruitment desk.
research_questions: What share of posted vacancies differ from the signed role template?
How many supervision meetings have no written case list?

already_counted.description: Manager edits vacancy lines that are not in the template
Interview time stays with the manager
Hire decision and supervision time stay with the manager

incremental.description: Update the role template when a site type is added
Staff resubmit a case list the meeting form rejects

approvals.approved_version: vacancy version signed for this role id
offer version signed for this candidate id

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes role templates are incomplete, so vacancies are still written by hand and only the offer send is new. The high case assumes the template is used, but every interview, every hire decision and every supervision meeting still takes the manager's time. No automated hiring is in scope.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Interviews, crisis calls, strategy choices and hiring stay with the manager. The change is a case file, a crisis pack, a loss brief and a vacancy that are ready before the conversation.
reach: Investigators open the interview on a fact list instead of a blank page.
Store supervisors can see which loss strategy version applies to their store.
skills_to_grow: Keep an interview as questions tied to logged facts, not a score of the person.
File a crisis recommendation as a version the store can be talked through.
Separate a hire decision from the vacancy form, with no trait score.
role.ambitious_version: Every suspected-theft interview has a signed outcome, every crisis plan has a review date, and every vacancy has a human hire decision.
